{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Sauce|Sauce]]

This '''chicken barbecue sauce''' is a [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]] based sauce used as marinade or barbecue sauce for grilled [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] parts such as wings, drumsticks or breasts. It also works very well for vegetarian (e.g., wheat- and soy-based) meat alternatives. It was invented by Johan Zandin from Gothenburg, Sweden and mixes 9 different ingredients from Europe, Asia and North America.

==Ingredients==
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] (30 [[Cookbook:mL|mL]]) [[Cookbook:Peanut Oil|peanut oil]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] (5 [[Cookbook:mL|mL]]) walnut oil
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] (30 [[Cookbook:mL|mL]]) mild [[Cookbook:Chili Paste|chili sauce]] (the kind just slightly hotter than ketchup)
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] (5 [[Cookbook:mL|mL]]) [[Cookbook:Worcestershire Sauce|Worcestershire sauce]] (see below for vegetarian alternative)
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] (5 [[Cookbook:mL|mL]]) [[Cookbook:Teriyaki|teriyaki]] marinade
*2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] (10 [[Cookbook:mL|mL]]) tandoori powder
*2 [[Cookbook:mL|mL]] ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|white pepper]]
*2 [[Cookbook:mL|mL]] [[Cookbook:Salt|herbal salt]]
*1 small, dried, crunched piri-piri [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile pepper]]

==Procedure==
#Mix everything together in a small [[Cookbook:Mixing bowl|mixing bowl]].
#Use a brush to apply a thick layer of the sauce to your favorite chicken parts or vegetarian alternative.
#[[Cookbook:Barbecue|Barbecue]] chicken over fire, charcoal or in the oven.
==Notes, tips and variations==
*The sauce can also be used as a [[Cookbook:Marinade|marinade]]: Soak the chicken parts in it, for half an hour to a few hours.
*Any remaining sauce can be applied with the brush during the cooking.
*In case of allergies or problems to find some ingredient, most ingredients can be replaced by similar alternatives:
**Peanut oil → [[Cookbook:Sunflower Oil|sunflower oil]], [[Cookbook:Corn Oil|corn oil]] or any other neutral oil
**Walnut oil → [[Cookbook:Sesame Oil|sesame oil]]
**Mild chili sauce → [[Cookbook:Ketchup|ketchup]] or [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato purée]]
**Worcestershire sauce → HP sauce
**Teriyaki marinade → [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]]
**Herbal salt → plain salt
**Piri-piri → any other hot [[Cookbook:Chili pepper|chili pepper]]

==Warnings==
*Make sure that any sauce that has been in contact with raw chicken gets properly heated. So do not apply more sauce just before taking the chicken from the heat or use the sauce uncooked after you have dipped the brush in it.
*Note that Worcestershire sauce usually is non-vegetarian, since at least the original recipe contains [[Cookbook:Anchovy|anchovies]]. (See above for alternative.)
